name: Spryker
title: Spryker SvelteKit Storefront — Svelte Commerce Connector
description: Svelte Commerce on Spryker’s Glue API: 25 of 43 services wired, with cart and sign-in, but the storefront cannot place an order yet. Setup and limits.
lede: Spryker’s storefront API speaks JSON:API, and the connector wires browsing, cart, sign-in and Spryker’s checkout data. The storefront cannot place an order on it yet: Spryker has no per-gateway checkout, and the storefront asks for one.
verdict: Browsing, cart and sign-in are wired, but the storefront cannot complete an order yet. Spryker has two checkout endpoints and no per-gateway ones, with payment methods named per store. The connector offers `getCheckoutData()` and `placeOrder()` for that, but the storefront’s payment step calls one method per gateway — cash on delivery included — and each of those is a placeholder.

quickStart.text: one connector at a time: remove the two the storefront ships with, add this one
point it at your Spryker Glue API

env.name: PUBLIC_SPRYKER_API_URL
env.note: Base URL of your Spryker Glue storefront API. Boot fails, naming this variable, if it is missing.

env.name: PUBLIC_SPRYKER_STORE_ID
env.note: The Spryker store name, sent as the `Store` header — `DE`, for example — for Dynamic Multistore.

env.name: PUBLIC_SPRYKER_ANONYMOUS_CUSTOMER_ID
env.note: A guest identity replayed as `X-Anonymous-Customer-Unique-Id`. The browser mints its own; this exists for server rendering.

env.name: PUBLIC_SPRYKER_NAVIGATION_KEY
env.note: The key for `GET /navigations/{key}`: Spryker has no route that lists navigations.

env.name: PUBLIC_SPRYKER_ACCESS_TOKEN
env.note: Sent as a bearer token when set.

env.name: PUBLIC_CONNECTOR
env.note: Only when more than one connector is installed: `@misiki/spryker-connector` names the one this build runs on.

envNote: `init.ts` hands the connector every `PUBLIC_SPRYKER_*` variable that is set, camel-cased: `PUBLIC_SPRYKER_ANONYMOUS_CUSTOMER_ID` arrives as `anonymousCustomerId`. The guide also lists `PUBLIC_SPRYKER_API_KEY`, `PUBLIC_SPRYKER_API_SECRET`, `PUBLIC_SPRYKER_ACCESS_KEY` and `PUBLIC_SPRYKER_CHANNEL_ID`; the connector’s source does not read them.
backendSettings: Name the store in `PUBLIC_SPRYKER_STORE_ID` if you run Dynamic Multistore: it travels as the `Store` header.
howItWorks: Spryker’s Glue storefront API answers in JSON:API, and the connector ships a deserialiser that resolves `included` relationships (the `jsonapi` file in its source is that helper, not a service). The store travels as a `Store` header, the locale as `Accept-Language`, and a guest as `X-Anonymous-Customer-Unique-Id`.

Checkout in Spryker is two calls: `POST /checkout-data`, which says what is still missing and which payment and shipment methods this cart can use, and `POST /checkout`, which places the order. Payment is chosen by method and provider names configured per store. The connector wires both as `getCheckoutData()` and `placeOrder()`; the storefront’s per-gateway methods stay placeholders, because inventing them would mean guessing a store’s payment method names.
limitations: The storefront cannot place an order. Checkout counts as wired because the connector reaches Spryker’s checkout endpoints, but the storefront’s payment step calls one method per gateway — cash on delivery, Razorpay, Stripe and the rest — and on Spryker each of those is a placeholder. The connector’s `getCheckoutData()` and `placeOrder()` are not called by the storefront yet.

faq.q: Can I run a Spryker store on Svelte Commerce today?
faq.a: Not to take orders. Browsing, cart and sign-in are wired, but the storefront’s payment step calls per-gateway methods that are placeholders on Spryker. The connector has the Spryker-native `getCheckoutData()` and `placeOrder()`; the storefront does not call them yet.

faq.q: How do I switch Svelte Commerce to Spryker?
faq.a: Remove the connectors the storefront ships with, install `@misiki/spryker-connector`, set `PUBLIC_SPRYKER_API_URL` in `.env` and start the dev server. `vite.config.ts` resolves whichever connector is installed, so no file in the storefront changes.

faq.q: Why can’t Svelte Commerce place an order on Spryker?
faq.a: Spryker has exactly two checkout endpoints — one to check what is missing, one to place the order — and chooses payment by names each store configures. The storefront expects one method per gateway, and inventing those would mean guessing a store’s payment method names, so the connector leaves them as placeholders.

api.surface: The connector calls Spryker’s Glue Storefront API, a JSON:API surface with no path prefix (`/catalog-search`, `/abstract-products/{sku}`, `/carts`, `/checkout` and so on hang off the configured host), and only its `POST /token` route takes form-encoded input and answers in flat JSON.
api.auth: A shopper signs in with an OAuth password grant to `POST /token`, sent as `application/x-www-form-urlencoded`, and the access token is then sent as `Authorization: Bearer <token>` and renewed once with the refresh token when a call answers 401; a guest is identified only by `X-Anonymous-Customer-Unique-Id`, which the connector mints itself and keeps in `localStorage` and a cookie.

calls.what: `GET /catalog-search` with `q`, `page`, `ipp`, `sort` and `category` for lists, and `GET /abstract-products/{sku}?include=concrete-products,abstract-product-image-sets,abstract-product-prices,abstract-product-availabilities` for one product, after `GET /url-resolver?url=` turns a slug into the SKU
`GET /category-trees` and `GET /category-nodes/{nodeId}`, with `GET /url-resolver?url=` for a category slug

`GET /carts` or `/guest-carts` with `include=items` or `guest-cart-items`, `POST /carts/{uuid}/items` or `POST /guest-cart-items`, `PATCH` on `{root}/{uuid}/{items|guest-cart-items}/{groupKey}`, and `POST {root}/{uuid}/vouchers`
`POST /checkout-data?include=payment-methods` for the current cart, since there is no standalone payment-methods route
`POST /token` (`grant_type=password`), then `GET /customers` for the profile; `POST /customers` to register and `DELETE /refresh-tokens/{token}` on sign-out

rules: `/catalog-search` pages with `page` and `ipp` and is the only route that reports a real total (`pagination.numFound`); `/orders` and the other offset routes take `page[offset]` and `page[limit]` and return only `links`, so their totals are worked out from `links.last`.

Sort values are mapped to the names Spryker’s search configuration publishes (`rating`, `name_asc`, `name_desc`, `price_asc`, `price_desc`, `popularity`), and the storefront default of newest first has no match and falls back to relevance.
Products are addressed by abstract SKU, so a storefront slug is resolved through `GET /url-resolver` before the detail call.

Registered shoppers and guests use separate cart trees that are not interchangeable (`/carts` with `items` against `/guest-carts` with `guest-cart-items`), line items are addressed by their `groupKey`, and a guest’s first `POST /guest-cart-items` creates the cart.
Registration with `POST /customers` does not sign the shopper in: Spryker mails a registration key and issues no token until it is confirmed through `POST /customer-confirmation`.
